# Backlog pruning

Every backlog needs pruning like an orchard does. Features nobody asked about for months are dead wood: they still take attention in every planning and compete with the work that bears fruit. Cutting back is uncomfortable, but it sends the team's vigour towards the few branches that matter.

My rule: each quarter I go through the list and remove whatever is older than six months and has no owner and no customer. What remains gets more room and more care. Pruning also protects the schedule, because a smaller scope is easier to finish.

Cut back early and cut hard, rather than late and in panic.
